g.text: Aisleflow against the three published lifelong planners

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: Taller is better: tasks delivered per 1000 timesteps of simulated time, same job stream and same robot count for every planner on a map.

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: Whiskers are 95% bootstrap intervals over 5 seeds. Each map is a different traffic problem, named under its bars; compare planners within a map.

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: Above each rival bar is a permutation test against aisleflow on the same seeds: `n.s.` means the two are not separated at p < 0.05, which at five seeds is most of them.

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: Token Passing and TPTS are complete only on well-formed MAPD instances -- one parking endpoint per agent -- which none of these floors provides at these robot counts. The next figure sweeps

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: the robot count and shows where that assumption starts to bite.

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: † Token Passing and TP + task swaps rest an agent with no task where it stopped, and `corridors` offers 0 parking bays for 35 agents. Every one of its single-file runs

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: has an agent standing in it before the first task is handed out, so no path across the map can be planned at all. This is the completeness assumption failing, not a tie-break.

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781
